sentences.text: It is submitted that it is a case of consent between two adults.
Victim (PW-1) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63368 2 CRA-1667-2023 has admitted that she had met Manish near a public water tap.
Thereafter she started talking to Manish over phone.

Manish used to lure her in the name of marriage and stated that he would like to marry her because he had purchased some land from a tribal person and registry is not in his name, therefore, he can get that land transferred in her name after marriage.
It is submitted that on such assurance she had received phone call on 29.01.2017 and had left her home.
Therefore, giving a long story about how thinks moved and how she travelled with Manish and other two co- accused persons namely Rakesh Agrawal and Atul Agrawal.
She has admitted that she does not know her date of birth and her age was recorded in the school as per estimation.
3. Reading from the evidence of PW-2 mother of the victim and PW-4 father of the victim it is pointed out that both of them have admitted that they had no idea about date of birth of the victim.
In fact PW-4 father of the victim has admitted in his cross- examination that since 1997 his wife is with him.
He has also admitted that he had not obtained any birth certificate either from the village Kotwar or Gram Panchayat or Police Station in regard to the victim.
He has also admitted that date of birth of the victim is not known to her and it was recorded in the school record on estimation.

4. It is pointed out that PW-10 school teacher Shri Dinesh Singh has corroborated this evidence of the parents of the victim saying that no proof of age was produced at the time of admission in the school of the victim at Government Primary School, Behariya and date of birth was recorded on the basis of estimation.
5. It is further pointed out that PW-15 lady Dr. Richa Gupta was working as Medical Officer, District Hospital, Umaria has clearly stated

that she had referred the victim to a radiologist at District Hospital, Umaria and the dental surgeon for age determination but no such age determination report is on record and she has further stated that no definite opinion in regard to violation of privacy can be given as victim was habitual of sexual intercourse

. Thus, it is submitted that present is a case of consent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63368 3 CRA-1667-2023 between two consenting adults and therefore, in the light of the judgment of Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana (2010) 1 SCC 742, wherein it is held that in allegation of rape of minor prosecution not conducting examinations by dental surgeon or radiologist of prosecutrix in spite of being referred to for such examination by doctor then such circumstance will be adverse to the case of the prosecution.
6.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, PW-1 victim has admitted her friendship with the appellant.
She has admitted that she was talking to appellant on phone.
She has also admitted that she was lured in the name of marriage because appellant had purchased certain lands from a tribal person.
PW-2 mother of the victim admitted that she has no clue as to the date of birth of her own or that of the victim.
8. PW-4 father of the victim too has stated that date of birth of the victim was recorded as per estimation.
He had no idea about the date of birth of the victim or of his own.
He admitted that he had not obtained any certificate in regard to date of birth of the victim, who was born at home either from Kotwar or Gram Panchayat or from any Police Station.
9. PW-10 school teacher has admitted that the date of birth was recorded on the basis of estimation and no documentary evidence was produced in support of date of birth of the victim.
10. As far as PW-15 lady Dr. Gupta is concerned, she has stated that she has referred the patient for age determination to the concerned dentist and the radiologist at District Hospital, Umaria.
There is no report of any dentist or radiologist in regard to age determination so to corroborate or contradict the evidence of school teacher PW- 11.

When these facts are taken into consideration then in the light of judgment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:63368 4 CRA-1667-2023 of Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana (supra), despite being referred for radiological examination for age determination prosecution having failed to comply with the directives of the doctor and further failed to bring on record copy of ossification report etc., that circumstance is to be considered against the prosecution as they were trying to suppress the real age of the victim which was even otherwise under cloud.

12. And these facts are taken into consideration then victim being a consenting adult and had left her home in the name of marriage with the appellant, the consensual relationship between two adults will not fall within the definition of either abduction or kidnapping or violation of privacy against will.
Even otherwise prosecution has failed to prove that victim was a child as defined under POCSO Act, therefore, provisions of POCSO Act will not be applicable.
13. Thus, when tested impugned judgment of conviction having being not based any cogent evidence produced by the prosecution deserves to be set aside and is hereby set aside.
14. Accordingly, appeal is allowed and disposed of.
Appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.

15. It is informed by learned Public Prosecutor for State that two co-accused were absconding,
therefore, record be sent to the trial Court for the needful.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
